content: In Canada, if you experience side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. Precautions: Before starting cefprozil, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication, penicillins, or other cephalosporin antibiotics (e.g., cephalexin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. This medication may cause dizziness. Consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you are confident you can do so safely. Limit your intake of alcoholic beverages. Cefprozil may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if clearly necessary. Cefprozil passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Cefprozil may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as specific diabetic urine tests or blood glucose tests, potentially causing false results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, or dizziness. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection (oral or vaginal fungal infection). A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. However, seek immediate medical attention if you notice symptoms of a severe allergic reaction, such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Information Last Revised: August 2024.
